subject: Architecture
title: The Arch Bridge: Strength from Curves
description: One-minute skill: The Arch Bridge: Strength from Curves.

hook.text: An arch is the strongest shape in nature. Every stone in an arch is being squeezed, never stretched.

buildup.text: Arch bridges transfer weight outward and downward into the abutments anchored in the ground.

discovery.text: The keystone at the top locks the arch together. Remove it, and the entire structure collapses instantly.

twist.text: Romans built stone arches 2,000 years ago. Some still carry traffic today without any structural repairs.

climax.text: Modern steel arches span up to 1,800 feet — the New River Gorge Bridge held the record for decades.

punchline.text: Curves beat straight lines. That's not art — that's physics.

quiz.question: What is the keystone's role in an arch bridge?
options: It decorates the highest point of the arch
It locks all the other stones together at the top
It allows water to drain through the structure
